protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS Real DoS: with server-side SNI enabled, Netty SniHandler calls SSLHelper.serverNameMapper which on non-null SNI does sslContextMaps[idx].computeIfAbsent(serverName, ...) into unbounded ConcurrentHashMap<String,SslContext>. Wildcard/broad cert mappings make distinct matching names all succeed, so an unauthenticated client can grow retained SslContext objects. GHSA-3g76-f9xq-8vp6 (not withdrawn) and CVE-2026-6860 cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED (CNA Eclipse, datePublished 2026-05-06) describe this; vendor blogs for 4.5.27/5.0.12 cite PR 6102/6103 as CVE-2026-6860. Parent SSLProviderImpl instead keyed by Certificate (computeIfAbsent(mgr.getCertificateChain(null)[0], ...)), so wildcard names collapsed to one cert and did not grow unbounded.

findings: CVE-2026-6860 is PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn). GHSA-3g76-f9xq-8vp6 withdrawn_at is null. Mechanism is CWE-770-style unbounded SNI SslContext cache growth, not a false positive.

BIC 58238be403a9a073aeaa47813bf0151ac1ff0d14 first writes SSLHelper sslContextMaps as ConcurrentHashMap keyed by serverName and populate via computeIfAbsent(serverName, ...); parent b83f2c1f2e358d8e66c193675b68398267472dbd used a Certificate-keyed map in SSLProviderImpl, which does not retain a distinct context per matching SNI name.

Source-to-sink at the BIC: HttpServerWorker/NetServerImpl construct SniHandler(sslHelper.serverNameMapper(vertx)); mapper calls createContext(..., serverName, ...); non-null names hit the unbounded map. Distinct wildcard-matching SNI names therefore accumulate SslContext entries.
